backlog.spec: After building the jittered staggered hex start in _solve_once, compute the bounding box of its points. Apply an independent affine stretch in x and in y so that the points span [0.06, 0.94] in each axis, using rng-drawn stretch factors only if the box is degenerate. Then run SLSQP as before. This removes the empty border that the fixed hex spacing leaves, while keeping the same row structure.
backlog.title: Affine stretch of the hex start to fill the square

backlog.spec: Reserve the last 10% of the time. Restarts use 0.7 of the time and the best raw SLSQP result is then re-optimised for the remaining time with ftol=1e-13 and maxiter 1000, starting from its centres and radii shrunk by 0.2%. Repair the result and keep it only if it beats the best.
backlog.title: Final tight polish of the best packing

backlog.spec: Combine the two best within-noise results (slots 6 and 19, both -2.9396). In _solve_once, give SLSQP an analytic objective gradient (zeros for the centres, -1 for the radii) and a dense analytic constraint Jacobian. For pair rows d_ij - r_i - r_j, the centre-i entries are (c_i - c_j)/d_ij, the centre-j entries are the negative of that, and the r_i and r_j entries are -1. Wall rows and r >= 0 rows get the obvious +-1 entries. Before calling SLSQP, relax the jittered hex centres with 30 L-BFGS-B iterations (bounds [0.03, 0.97]) on the energy sum over pairs of max(0, 2*INIT_RADIUS*1.6 - d_ij)^2, using an analytic gradient. Leave everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Combine analytic Jacobian with L-BFGS-B pre-relaxation

backlog.spec: Instead of drawing the row count R uniformly from {5,6,7} on every restart, keep per-R statistics: the best and the mean repaired radius sum seen so far. Give each R three restarts first, then pick R by a simple UCB rule (mean sum + 0.01*sqrt(log(total)/count_R)), or equivalently sample R with probability proportional to exp((best_R - best_overall)/0.003). Pass R into _solve_once as an argument; everything else (jitter, random subset, SLSQP, repair) is unchanged. All randomness must still come from the seeded rng. The aim is to spend the restarts on the row count that yields the top basin.
backlog.title: Bandit over hex-grid row counts

backlog.spec: Pass options={'maxiter': MAX_ITER, 'ftol': 1e-9} to the SLSQP call in _solve_once instead of the default ftol of 1e-6. The default tolerance can stop runs before they converge to their local optimum, which loses about 1e-4 to 1e-3 of radius sum per run and can also misrank candidates. Change nothing else.
backlog.title: Tighter SLSQP tolerance in restarts

backlog.spec: The hex grid has R*m >= n positions, and the surplus is now dropped by a random permutation. Change only which positions are dropped. Per restart choose one of three modes with equal probability: (a) drop only boundary positions (first or last row, first or last column), chosen at random; (b) drop only interior positions, chosen at random; (c) the current uniform random choice. If a mode has fewer eligible positions than the surplus, fill the rest uniformly at random. Keep the jitter, the clip, the row-count draw, SLSQP and the repair unchanged. The aim is to learn whether vacancy placement decides which basin SLSQP falls into; record the mode of the best run in a comment-free variable so that the next edit can fix the winning mode.
backlog.title: Vacancies of the hex grid placed on purpose

backlog.spec: In solve, keep a per-R record (R in 5, 6, 7) of the best repaired radius sum found from starts with that row count. Pass R into _solve_once instead of drawing it there. For the first 9 restarts, cycle R through 5, 6, 7. After that, pick R with probability proportional to exp((best_R - global_best)/0.003), and always give each R at least 10 percent probability. Use the seeded rng for all draws. This spends more restarts on the lattice type that is producing the best basins.
backlog.title: Adaptive row-count bandit

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, draw an extra e = rng.integers(0, 2), and use m = ceil(n/R) + e columns, so there are R*m positions. The spacing stays (m + 0.5) in x, as in the current formula. Then take a random subset of n positions as now. With e = 1 there are more empty sites and a slightly denser lattice, which gives different hole patterns. Everything else, including the jitter and clipping, is unchanged.
backlog.title: Spare grid columns for subset selection

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, with k = rng.integers(0, 4), take n - k jittered hex-grid positions as now. Place the remaining k circles at random interstitial points: the midpoints of random triples of neighbouring grid points, or random points near the walls, chosen with the seeded rng. Give the main circles an initial radius of INIT_RADIUS and the interstitial ones 0.02. Then run SLSQP as before. Optimal packings for n=32 usually contain a few small rattler-like circles in gaps, and this init starts them there directly.
backlog.title: Interstitial small circles in the init

backlog.spec: After 60% of the time, build children from two of the top 5 distinct packings: take the circles with centre x<t from parent A and those with x>=t from parent B, with t random in [0.3,0.7]. Fix the count to n by dropping the smallest or adding random points. Run SLSQP on the child and keep it in the pool if it is good.
backlog.title: Elite crossover of halves

backlog.spec: Replace SLSQP in _solve_once with a trust-region successive LP that uses scipy.optimize.linprog (method='highs'). Start from the same hex-grid init. At each iteration linearise the pair constraints d_ij - r_i - r_j >= 0 around the current centres, only for pairs with d_ij < 0.45, keep the wall constraints (already linear), and solve an LP in the steps (dc, r) that maximises sum(r) subject to |dc| <= delta per coordinate. Start with delta = 0.05. Accept the step if the exactly repaired radius sum of the new centres improves, otherwise halve delta. Stop when delta < 1e-7 or after 80 iterations. Build the constraint matrix as a scipy.sparse matrix. Keep the restart loop and the final repair, and check process_time inside the SLP loop so that solve() never passes TIME_FRACTION * time_limit.
backlog.title: Successive linear programming as the local solver

backlog.spec: Build the start configuration greedily. Place circles one at a time: at each step, evaluate a 50x50 grid of candidate points, and choose the point that maximises min(distance to placed centres minus their radii, distance to the walls). Set that clearance as the new circle's radius, with the first circle's radius at 0.1, and continue to n circles. Randomise the candidate grid with rng (small random offset per restart). Feed the resulting centres and radii to SLSQP as the start, and keep the repair step.
backlog.title: Sequential greedy maximal-hole init

backlog.spec: Use an objective -sum(r) in a first SLSQP stage of 60 iterations. In that stage add 0.5*sum(r^2) so that the radii are more equal and the packing stays spread out. Then rerun SLSQP with the pure -sum(r) objective from that point for the remaining iterations.
backlog.title: Decaying small-radius weight objective

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, draw n + k hex-grid points with k = rng.integers(1, 4), using the same jittered staggered grid but taking a random subset of n + k positions (raise m if needed). Run SLSQP with maxiter 60 on all n + k circles. Drop the k circles with the smallest radii, then run SLSQP with MAX_ITER on the remaining n circles, starting from their centres and current radii. This lets the optimizer choose which grid holes stay empty, instead of picking them at random.
backlog.title: Overfill and prune init

backlog.spec: Make no functional change beyond the current train.py (hex-grid init). Only change a harmless constant such as the rng seed offset: use np.random.default_rng(seed + 1000). This gives a replicate measurement of the incumbent's true loss, so later gains can be judged against noise.
backlog.title: Replicate slot 0 baseline

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, first run SLSQP for 100 iterations with the objective -sum(w * r), where w_i = 1 + 0.03 * rng.normal() is drawn per circle. Then run SLSQP again from that result with the true objective -sum(r) for MAX_ITER iterations. The random weights break the symmetry between circles of equal size, push some circles to grow and others to shrink, and so help escape near-symmetric saddle configurations that a uniform-radius start tends to fall into.
backlog.title: Randomly weighted first pass then unweighted pass

backlog.spec: After SLSQP and clipping, for each circle whose gap to a wall is below 0.02, move its centre so that it touches that wall (set the coordinate to r, or 1-r). Then run the existing repair. This closes small wall gaps that SLSQP leaves through its tolerance and gives radii a little more room. Keep the SLSQP call and the time-limit loop unchanged.
backlog.title: Snap-to-boundary post-processing before repair

backlog.spec: In each restart, generate a batch of 8 candidate initial centre sets using the current hex-init procedure with the seeded rng. For each one, compute a cheap score: the sum over all circles of min(distance to the nearest wall, half the distance to the nearest neighbour), which is a feasible radius estimate, vectorised with numpy. Run SLSQP only on the candidate with the highest score. The scoring costs about a millisecond, so the restart rate barely changes, while starts with clumped or overlapping jitter are filtered out.
backlog.title: Batch prescreen inits by a cheap energy

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, replace the hex-grid start with a square lattice of about n+4 points (ceil(sqrt(n+4)) columns and rows, spaced evenly over [0.05, 0.95]). Pick n of them uniformly at random with rng, then add N(0, 0.01) jitter and clip to [0.03, 0.97]. Keep the initial radius at INIT_RADIUS and leave the SLSQP call and repair unchanged. Use the seed only through rng.
backlog.title: Square-lattice init with random deletions

backlog.spec: With probability 0.5 per restart, replace the hex-grid init with a greedy construction; otherwise use the current init. Build a fixed 40x40 grid of candidate points in the square. Place circles one at a time: for every candidate compute the largest radius allowed by the walls and the already-placed circles (min of wall distance and centre distance minus placed radius), cap it at a value drawn uniformly from [0.07, 0.12], then pick a candidate at random among the 5 with the largest allowed radius and place the circle there. After n circles, start SLSQP from these centres with initial radii of 0.8 times the greedy radii (floored at 0.01). Vectorise the candidate evaluation with numpy so that the construction costs a few milliseconds.
backlog.title: Greedy largest-hole constructive init

memo:
Helped: only the init change in slot 0 (jittered staggered hex grid, 5-7 rows, random subset of positions): -2.9253 to -2.9375 (delta -0.0123), well above noise sd 0.0034. It is a single run, not yet replicated. Slots 6, 19 and 33 (-2.9396, delta -0.0020) are within noise, so they are possible but unconfirmed. Slot 31 (-0.0005) is noise.
Did not help: schedule edits (2-4, 7, 13, 23-25), bounds (1), analytic gradients alone (5), trust-constr polish (8), restarting from best or a pool (9, 11, 22, 28), random radii (10, 14), pair pruning (12), screening (17), swap moves (29), LP repair (34), and other hex-init variants (15, 16, 18, 21, 27, 32). These ranged from +0.0006 to +0.0087.
Next: replicate slot 0 once. Then combine it with slot 6 (analytic gradient and Jacobian) and slot 19 or 33 (L-BFGS-B pre-relaxation). Skip schedule and repair changes. Treat gains under 0.003 as noise.
